title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: users can upload local and OneDrive files to custom engine agents
summary: Hold: the checklist presents tenant-wide User access as a way to restrict selected agents, which could unintentionally restrict access to all agents and plugins. The page also asserts that uploaded-file storage, retention and logging depend solely on agent code, although Microsoft has not documented those boundaries for this planned feature. The roadmap facts and the cited control endpoints are supported.

claims.claim: Unsupported chat attachments mean no document leaves the user's device or OneDrive through that route today.

Do not infer a transport or data-boundary guarantee from unsupported functionality.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: Storage, retention and logging of uploaded files depend on the agent's code rather than any Microsoft control.
claims.quote: Searched: "custom engine agents" "files" "retention" storage upload permissions sensitivity labels. Opened known-issues, agents-overview and cost-considerations; read custom engine overview privacy excerpts. No source establishes these exclusive boundaries for planned uploads.
claims.fix: Replace 'Where the file is stored, retained or logged depends on that agent's code, not on a Microsoft control' with 'Microsoft has not documented the storage, retention, logging or Microsoft governance coverage for files supplied through this planned upload capability. Ask each agent owner to explain its downstream processing and controls.' Recast 'the agent's own code decides what happens next' as a risk to assess, not an exclusive governance fact.
